newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET TIGHT, RATES STABLE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET TIGHT, RATES STABLE.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted stable on Wednesday despite a slight shortage of cash, dealers said.
They said the market opened with a Z$86.7 million deficit and no maturities were anticipated during the day. Hence the central Reserve Bank was not auctioning any treasury bills on Wednesday.
Meanwhile, treausury bills were being traded on the secondary market at a stable 24.65 percent as was call money at 22 percent.
Bankers acceptance bills were also unchanged at 25.35 percent (buying) and at 24.85 (selling).
The buying rate quoted for 30-, 60- and 90-day NCD bills was stable at 26 percent and they were also being sold at a steady 25.5 percent.
